data.narrative:
Q-CTRL is a Series B quantum computing software company founded by Michael Biercuk that has raised $132M to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 3 public comps (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable here, using the $132M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the next stage, yielding $251M. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable: while 5 same-sector peers exist, none satisfy the minimum threshold of 3 datapoints when filtered by same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier criteria. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce excessive noise given the heterogeneity of quantum computing company business models and technology platforms.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $213M to $288M, with a median estimate of $251M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficiently granular peer comparables at Q-CTRL's specific stage and the variance in quantum computing peer valuations driven by different technology approaches (gate-based, annealing, photonic) and go-to-market models. Additional disclosure of Q-CTRL's revenue or customer metrics would enable revenue multiple triangulation.
